findings.text: blocking: the carried points are written onto the run's still-queued review while _charge_points marks the delivered run as holding the same points (queue_edit.py:669), so both records count under the one session and a 4-point raise reports 4 for the run plus 4 for its review; reproduced in a scratch tree at b7884a4b93ab with a delivered run, its queued review and its promotion request: session_priority_in_use() read 8 with holders ['r1', 'review-of-r1'] immediately after reprioritise(run, 4), so a session at its budget is refused work it could afford, and after the run lands the review still holds the points the evidence page says returned.

non-blocking: assert result["priority"] == 4 compares the argument the test handed reprioritise against the field reckon/crew/queue_edit.py:626 echoes back unconditionally, so it cannot fail for any change short of altering the return shape; the guards that matter in that test are the budget, promotion-override and drain-order assertions below it.

non-blocking: the gate ran in a scratch tree (/tmp/mcintos-landing-5372a109de75-wU53Ag/tree) but the manifest records no measurement_module or measurement_cwd line and the scoped-gate log's header names neither, so a later reader cannot tell which module the run imported.

item_verdicts.goal: the goal is that a run's priority carries to its review and its promotion; reckon/crew/queue_order.py:333 ranks two reviews by their run's points and reckon/crew/queue_edit.py:587 accepts a delivered run, so both halves of the goal landed.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_run_s_priority_carries_to_its_review_and_its_promotion.py:126 fails on any regression of the review ordering (proved by the base control) and :218 fails if the carry stops, but :174 asserts only the value reprioritise echoes back from its own argument (queue_edit.py:626), and no assertion covers the queued-review budget case named in the finding.
justifications.evidence: the gate log scoped-gate-1794982705627943931.log records 5 passed EXIT=0 at b7dd46560df6 and docs/evidence/fragments/a-session-.../s3.html quotes that summary line, but its MEASURE "session points in use=0" after landing holds only because no review was queued in that test, and the manifest's evidence_inputs records that the done-when's named negative-control case (promotion order) was already green at base.
justifications.fit: reckon/crew/queue_edit.py:639 follows the module's existing private-helper and docstring idiom, the new names are role nouns (_charge_points, _carry_points_to_queued_work, PRIORITY_DELIVERED_MARK at reckon/crew/runs.py:609) and carry no run or plan identifier.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/queue_order.py:333 orders reviews by their run's points and reckon/crew/queue_edit.py:672 writes a delivered run's raise onto its queued review and promotion request, but the raise charges the same points twice when the review is still queued (see the finding at queue_edit.py:705).
justifications.reuse: the review ordering reuses queue_order._override and the review composer's existing priority option (reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:4006), but reckon/crew/queue_edit.py:705 re-states the priority/priority_override write triple that reckon/crew/dispatching/requests.py:304, reckon/crew/promotion_requests.py:445 and reckon/crew/runs.py:1052 already write inline, rather than extending one writer.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in git diff --stat 8d870f62598f..b7884a4b93ab (reckon/crew/queue_edit.py, reckon/crew/queue_order.py, reckon/crew/runs.py, reckon/crew_run_commands.py, the flight schema source and its two generated copies, skills/reckon-build/SKILL.md, the test file and the two evidence pages) is inside the declared write paths.
